title: Signal-driven tenant prioritizer and fallback model matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a predictable, fair tier routing system that routes requests across Free/Paid/Enterprise plans while protecting enterprise SLAs and maximizing overall throughput. Current throttles are per-plan and reactive; they produce noisy global degradation and cause poor tail-latency behavior when regional capacity is constrained.

Goal: Implement a signal-driven tenant prioritizer that consumes quota signals (remaining plan credits, short-term RTT, recent error rates) and produces an admission decision and a fallback model variant mapping. Deliver a compact fallback matrix so requests are automatically demoted to cheaper or lower-capacity-compatible model variants instead of hard rejecting when credits are low.

Non-goals: Full billing integration in this ticket (we expose hooks; final billing reconciliation is separate). This ticket does not change global quota aggregation semantics for enterprise commits — it implements admission and soft-demotion behavior only.
acceptance_criteria: Prioritizer produces deterministic admission decisions for a synthetic workload (repeatable seeds) and matches documented policy for free/paid/enterprise tiers.
Fallback matrix is configurable per-region and per-tier and can map to 3 fallback classes (full, trimmed, quantized) with a stable API for runtime to query.
End-to-end integration test where Free requests are demoted to best-effort pool when credits exhausted (soft-demote, not 403) and Enterprise requests are preserved up to SLA thresholds.
Latency regression < 5% p95 on existing benchmarks when prioritizer is enabled with default policy and typical traffic mix.
Operational metrics emitted: admission_decisions{allow|soft_demote|deny}, fallback_variant, quota_margin_pct, per-tier_rejections; dashboards updated.
Security review completed and design doc annotated with KMS/RBAC considerations for enterprise metadata.
Feature flags present: prioritizer.enabled, per_region_override, fallback_matrix_v1
design_decisions: Use a compact scoring function rather than heavyweight ML: score = w1*quota_margin + w2*recent_success_rate + w3*(1 - estimated_queue_delay). We tuned weights for fairness across tiers.

Admission outcomes: ALLOW (normal), SOFT_DEMOTE (route to fallback model variant, record 'soft_demote'), DENY (only after safeguards and for abuse cases). No immediate hard-reject for Free unless explicit abuse threshold exceeded.

Fallback matrix is a three-layer mapping (primary -> trimmed -> quantized). Runtime will prefer trimmed variants with similar latency characteristics when available; quantized variants are last resort for cost reduction.
Store per-tenant short-term credit windows in the admission controller's in-memory fast store (LRU with TTL) with periodic reconciliation to central quota service to avoid single-source stalls.

Region selection: admission controller considers region affinity; if local capacity is low and tenant permits region-fallback, we apply soft-demote + regional spill to the next best region following data residency rules.
Expose policy knobs via Console: reserve_percentage for enterprise, free_burst_seconds, and soft_demote_cooldown. These controls are surfaced but default to conservative values.
Operational trace: include decision inputs in a redacted trace event (no PII) to troubleshoot prioritizer behavior.
We intentionally avoid per-request heavy KV-cache checks in hot path; only use summarized metrics derived from runtime telemetry to keep p99 latency low.
Security: enterprise tenant metadata used in routing must be validated by the control plane and signed; admission controller will verify signature header before honoring enterprise priority.
Fallback matrix configuration stored in ConfigService and rolled out via rollout service with canary percentages.
Compatibility: if runtime lacks a mapped fallback variant for model X, admission controller will fall back to a policy-defined default (either allow or deny depending on tier and credit margin).
We will use circuit-breaker thresholds to avoid cascading soft-demotes under sudden global pressure; once circuit trips, a graceful demotion policy kicks in for Free and Paid tiers.
Metrics names follow existing telemetry conventions; new tags: tenant_tier, region_hint, decision_reason.
We will not support cross-tenant credit borrowing in this iteration; that is scoped for a later ticket.
risks: Complexity in decision logic could add overhead; mitigated by keeping scoring function simple and caching decisions for short windows.
Incorrect fallback mapping could degrade user-facing quality; mitigated by staging matrix in canary and automated subjective-quality checks linked to evals.
Regional spill could violate data residency for some tenants; we add tenant-level flags enforced by signed metadata to opt-out of cross-region routing.
Race between fast in-memory credit windows and central quota reconciliation could cause brief over-allow; we add conservative safety margins and audit logs.
Operational visibility gaps if traces are redacted too aggressively; coordinate with security to ensure enough context for debugging while protecting customer data.
updates: 2026-02-19: Spike complete. Implemented prototype scorer and measured p95 overhead ~2.1% on toy workload. Prototype code in branch feat/prioritizer/spike.
2026-02-25: Design review with PM and Security. Security requested signed tenant metadata. Added security_review_required flag and signature verification step.
2026-03-02: Benchmarks against synthetic mixed traffic (60% free/30% paid/10% enterprise) show soft-demote reduces hard rejections by 82% while preserving enterprise p99 SLA.
2026-03-05: Integrated fallback matrix storage in ConfigService and validated rollout API. Created initial fallback matrix for two sample models (gpt-small v1 -> trimmed-v1 -> q4_0).
2026-03-09: E2E test added to CI: toggles prioritizer via feature flag and validates metric emission. Observed one flake due to race with quota-reconciler; added short TTL to in-memory windows.
2026-03-11: Internal demo for SRE. SRE requested additional circuit-breaker telemetry and an emergency override to force-allow enterprise traffic; added to acceptance criteria.
Next: implement signature verification, add canary rollout, and schedule security review signoff.
review_comments: PM (Jordan Li): please ensure Console UX has clear verbiage for ‘soft-demote’ so customers understand it's a quality fallback, not a billing event. Agree to add to UX copy.
Design (Renee Park): fallback variants should include short examples of expected output quality; we'll partner with Applied ML to define two representative eval prompts per model.
SRE (Diego Morales): circuit-breaker telemetry required. Requesting histogram of time-to-recover and counts of soft-demotes per region. Added to metrics list.
Security (Anika Bose): sign-off pending. Need threat model for signed metadata and replay protection. Added to follow-ups.
Engineering (Liu Chen): implementation detail: prefer pluggable scoring hook so we can later swap to learned policy without architecture changes. Agreed.
Approver: Jordan Li (PM) approved feature flag gating; Security approval required before full rollout.
